questions.stem: This clinician is palpating deeply in the mid-abdomen above the umbilicus in a patient with suspected aortic aneurysm. What physical finding is being sought?

explanation.summary: A pulsatile, expansile mass palpated above the umbilicus suggests an AAA; below that level the aorta has bifurcated into the common iliac arteries.
explanation.whyCorrect: A pulsatile, expansile mass palpated above the umbilicus suggests an AAA; below that level the aorta has bifurcated into the common iliac arteries.

questions.stem: Bedside ultrasound is preferred over CT for a hypotensive patient with a suspected ruptured AAA primarily because it:

choices.label: B
choices.text: Can be performed at the bedside without transporting an unstable patient

choices.label: D
choices.text: Has higher spatial resolution than CT

choices.label: E
choices.text: Better visualizes the retroperitoneum than CT

explanation.summary: In an unstable, hypotensive patient, point-of-care ultrasound rapidly confirms an aneurysm at the bedside, avoiding the risk of transporting the patient to the radiology department.
explanation.whyCorrect: In an unstable, hypotensive patient, point-of-care ultrasound rapidly confirms an aneurysm at the bedside, avoiding the risk of transporting the patient to the radiology department.

questions.stem: CT angiography is considered the gold-standard imaging modality for evaluating an aortic aneurysm chiefly because it is the most effective tool for:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Detailed anatomic assessment and pre-operative planning

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bedside evaluation of an unstable, hypotensive patient

choices.label: C
choices.text: Avoiding the need for IV contrast

explanation.summary: CT angiography provides the detailed anatomy needed for pre-operative planning in stable patients; the hypotensive patient is more safely evaluated with bedside ultrasound.
explanation.whyCorrect: CT angiography provides the detailed anatomy needed for pre-operative planning in stable patients; the hypotensive patient is more safely evaluated with bedside ultrasound.

questions.stem: This chest X-ray finding was discovered incidentally in a patient later found to have a thoracic aortic aneurysm. Such an aneurysm can also compress an adjacent nerve, producing which symptom?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve compression

explanation.summary: A thoracic aortic aneurysm may show mediastinal widening on X-ray and can compress the recurrent laryngeal nerve, causing hoarseness, or compress the trachea/esophagus.
explanation.whyCorrect: A thoracic aortic aneurysm may show mediastinal widening on X-ray and can compress the recurrent laryngeal nerve, causing hoarseness, or compress the trachea/esophagus.

questions.stem: This CT shows an abdominal aortic aneurysm surrounded by inflammatory change with pockets of gas (black foci) in the wall. What does the presence of gas indicate?

explanation.summary: Periaortic inflammation with gas points to an infected (mycotic) aneurysm; these are rare but life-threatening and require prompt antibiotics plus surgical resection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Periaortic inflammation with gas points to an infected (mycotic) aneurysm; these are rare but life-threatening and require prompt antibiotics plus surgical resection.

questions.stem: This illustration depicts an aneurysm involving the aortic root and ascending aorta. Distortion of the aortic root here most characteristically produces which auscultatory finding?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Systolic ejection murmur of aortic stenosis

explanation.summary: Dilation at the aortic root pulls the aortic valve leaflets apart, causing aortic regurgitation, which is heard as a high-pitched, blowing, decrescendo diastolic murmur.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dilation at the aortic root pulls the aortic valve leaflets apart, causing aortic regurgitation, which is heard as a high-pitched, blowing, decrescendo diastolic murmur.

questions.stem: This patient with a known abdominal aortic aneurysm developed acutely painful, cyanotic toes while palpable pulses were preserved. What is the underlying mechanism?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Occlusion of a large proximal artery

choices.label: E
choices.text: Distal embolization of mural thrombus from the aneurysm

explanation.summary: Turbulent flow in an aneurysm promotes mural thrombus, fragments of which can embolize distally to small digital vessels, producing blue toe syndrome with preserved proximal pulses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Turbulent flow in an aneurysm promotes mural thrombus, fragments of which can embolize distally to small digital vessels, producing blue toe syndrome with preserved proximal pulses.

questions.stem: Aneurysms of the artery behind the knee, illustrated here, most commonly cause which complication rather than rupture?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Thrombosis or distal embolization causing limb ischemia

explanation.summary: Popliteal aneurysms rarely rupture; instead their major complications are thrombosis occluding the artery or serving as a source of atheroemboli, causing distal leg ischemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Popliteal aneurysms rarely rupture; instead their major complications are thrombosis occluding the artery or serving as a source of atheroemboli, causing distal leg ischemia.
